after several weeks of running Meta ads and wathing the metrics, I think one of the biggest issues we face is the Cruise Brothers booking page/s itself.
The booking page and portal are designed with a real agent in mind first and foremost and cause a 'Deer in the headlights' situation for the average 'Facebook/AOL' crowd that fit's our desired demographic almost perfectly - if we can make it WAY MORE easy for them to book - more specifically, getting them through the super long data process for them and their guests, and to the final payment phase where we should try to considate any 'must have' Odysseus steps for the user to manage (I don't currently see any feasible way to completely remove Odysseus from the guest flow - but it would be nice!)
All  ideas should be grounded around the idea of just about all of our guests being 'technically' un-sophisticated, using their IPhone only, Boomer generation, Ready to purchase a ticket, and easily distracted!

I am considering using any combination of options including:
1. Voice chat to make getting required information easier for guests
2. Large, single value inputs (or minimal n-value forms) easy to read and input information
3. browser based data-collection that resumes if a guest accidentally changes the page.
4. Fast switching from voice to text and back.
5. Many of these concepts were originated already in our codebase for a more advanced chat system that we can borrow from for this. This includes the 'SKILL' based logic system we used. This new system will be far more limited in it's scope however - primarily focusing on getting the guest to the final payment page.
6. An option to 'request' an agent (Me) pick up wherevey they are at any time (by keeping track of everything implicitly and sending a quick link to me where I can continue if the process gets stuck)
7 . We will remove the 3 separate call-to-actions from the landing and just track 1 book now button that will contain all of the ways to start and/or complete a booking manually or with agent, AI or Human, at any point during the process.
8. 

We will hard store (dynamoDB) all info to quickly reference for future bookings with each guest, and LET THEM KNOW that we ONLY EVER ASK ANY QUESTION ONCE!


We are going to FIRST research (again) the full REST flow for Odysseus http calls and develop the rules/system for automating the correct fields to progress the booking flow.
Important correction: Odysseus is not REST end-to-end. Search and discovery use JSON calls under `/nitroapi/v2/`, but the booking flow changes to stateful ASP.NET form posts tied to cookies, hidden server state, and a short-lived `brn`. Our durable guest workflow must live in DynamoDB, while a controlled browser session creates or recreates the current Odysseus booking state and stops at payment.

The current research map, known endpoints, field-automation rules, missing capture steps, resume strategy, and safe capture command are documented in:




- Start booking now (we will walk you through it!)
The process should always begin by taking the user information: first name, phone number, and email. With that email and name, we can immediately start emailing them any specific information that we need to acquire. With the phone number, the guest can at any time hit the 'FINISH NOW!' button to request an agent to call them immediately! The link that is sent to me should take me to a dash with all accepted info and the fields for whats left for me to fill, a live link to the booking page for a side by side workflow, and the suggested next steps to completing the booking!
- once we have their email and more info, and once they leave the page or stop activity for more than an hour, we automatically send them an email witht he remaining fields, based on the info we have about the number of guests we know about - always proceeding forward with what we know
I am considering a branch of the process that takes any collected information, figures out what remaining information needs to be collected, and sends the user a very simple form to their email with only the required information to get them to the finished process. That would be one single branch that they can choose to take. 

##Order of data collection
-Name
-Email
-Phone
-Num guests
-Guest ages
- etc

continue to collect all needed info, store, and ultimately send the guest a final link for payment on Odysseus.

when collecting the phone number we need to get the users allowed intent by having them check 'Call' and or 'Text' as available contact options. No selection forces us to use email to contact them and use the phone only for the main guests phone field in the booking.
we also need to clearly and consicely (and in simple language) lay out what the guest can expect to see and fill-out on the booking page before they are finally sent there - when they are finally sent there (preferrably for payment only).

Our system should automatically track users that begin the booking flow and continually send email updates to complete their booking until it is finalized.




When building this new booking/CTA flow, it should be mobile first, and I want to start by prototyping the actual 'Flow' page to ensure that the process moves fluidly and easily for older guests.
Before implementing the complex logic, I wanna make sure that the user interaction and workflow are perfect. I want to be able to test using voice and switching to chat, filling in dynamic forms really quickly, asking miscellaneous questions, and just seeing the chat interface in its design and interaction abilities before we build out the complicated logic. 
The layout should provide a simple 'More Options' tab that display the different actions the user can take at any given point based on the data that has been collected up to that point. This means the first phase of the chat will simply be input boxes for email and name. As the form progresses, we can provide more options, like:
- having a user call me now because we have their number
- sending an email because we have their email
- and so forth
The booking flow will be extremely straightforward, providing options to the user only as the flow progresses, and starting with the single option of collecting the most basic info - regardless if requesting a callback or trying to complete the booking now, it all starts from the single entry point on the landing page that will lead to this new 'Flow' page we will now design.

The voice mode will basically emulate the chat mode but just add conversational voice functionality (see the original voice chat implementation in project)
(.github\DOCS\Implementation\BLUEPRINTS\CHAT_SYSTEM_BLUEPRINT.md)

I want to be able to tap-in, or 'pick-up' a started booking flow right from where I monitor the 'Curated Deals' in '/tests/deals-system'. I should be able to see everybody that entered the booking flow from the landing page, see all of the data they entered, and perform any number of actions like CALL THEM, email them, populate and complete the booking, generate the final booking link and send to their email, and anything else I am not thinking about yet.

We should incorporate AI where it is plausible to do things like figure out what questions to ask next and manage dynamically generated forms or form fields. 
We should let the user know to leave the page open and simply come back if they want to take a break and finish filling the form out later. 
We should also have a digital agent/AI agent that can be chatted with to ask really important questions on the fly without actually exiting the current flow process that we're on. So if the users are in the middle of filling out a particular part of the form, but they have a question about something completely different, they can simply hit a button, ask the AI, and get a side message answered quickly without ever exiting the flow. This has to be very elegantly presented, so we need to consider that old people will be using this. It needs to be easy to operate and very intuitive. 
The agent should be smart enough to be able to switch modes if necessary. For example, if we are asking the person to answer certain questions and the person wants to answer another set of questions, we can quickly dynamically switch to that set of questions. The goal here is to get all the important information that we need, not necessarily in any particular order, but whatever is convenient for the user. 

The notifications that I received now for callbacks will need to be upgraded because I'm going to need to get different levels of notifications, starting from:
- basic booking process started
- confirmations that are not urgent
- user needs help booking right now, which is urgent

What I'm thinking is the data input system will be a chat back and forth with the user. The chat agent will have a goal to collect a certain amount of information that it already has knowledge of and will do a combination of answering questions and taking information at the same time, making it a very fluid experience with the user. The agent will dynamically generate easy-to-read and fill-in form fields, not overwhelming the user, getting just enough information at any one particular time to keep the progression going forward and answering any basic questions to the user at the same time.

The best launch flow is: the assistant prepares everything, then you take over inside Odysseus for the time-sensitive and financial steps.
Booking Assistant preparation
Collect and verify legal passenger details, contact information, residency/address, cabin preferences, and stated service preferences. No live cabin timer yet.

Operator takeover
You receive a “Ready to book” packet, open Odysseus, and revalidate the current price and availability.

Cabin selection
You select the approved category and cabin. This starts the red-badge timer and likely temporary inventory state. Material price or cabin changes require customer approval.

Passenger autofill and review
Confirmed passenger data fills the Odysseus form. You verify names, DOB, nationality, gender/title, address, and contact details before continuing.

Booking Contact
The tested flow requires only Email and Phone. These can come from a saved, approved operator profile.

Services and insurance
Safe information such as residency country/state can autofill. Special occasions, tours, transfers, insurance, and other paid or consequential choices should reflect confirmed answers or receive your manual review—never silently invented.

Payment and final submission
You select the appropriate deposit/full-payment schedule, enter payment only within the Cruise Brothers-controlled page, review totals and terms, and manually perform the final submission. The assistant never handles card details.

Confirmation
Capture the confirmation number, reconcile the resulting CBAT Trip marked Imported From Odysseus, update the Booking Assistant record, and send the customer their confirmation.

Expect cabin timers, occasional price changes, supplier-specific fields, unavailable insurance, card declines, and sessions that must be restarted. The Share link remains useful as a fresh customer booking entry, but not as a prepared-checkout resume link.

Phase 0 now passes for this operator-assisted pilot model.

8:10 PM






so does this mean we CANNOT create the booking first and send the customer the final payment link? I will always have to take the payment card from the guest??






11:40 AM






No—the conclusion is narrower.
What we proved is that you cannot prepare checkout in your browser and send the customer that raw checkout.aspx?brn=... payment URL. It is bound to your browser session.
You would not always need to take the card. Three possibilities remain:
Customer self-service: send the Share link; the customer completes the booking and enters their card on their own device. They may restart at Stateroom or Guest Information.
Post-booking payment request: create a hold/unpaid booking, then send an official customer-payment link. We have not yet proven whether Cruise Brothers supports this—the experiments stopped before creating a booking.
Agent-assisted payment: you take the card using Cruise Brothers’ approved telephone-payment procedure and enter it directly into Odysseus. Never store it in the Booking Assistant or chat.
The exact unanswered question is now:
After an authorized hold or unpaid booking is created, does its CBAT booking record provide “Send Payment Link,” “Customer Payment,” or a guest-manage-booking URL?

That feature may also vary by cruise line and fare. We should verify it with Cruise Brothers documentation/support first, or through an explicitly authorized test hold. Until then, don’t assume you will always need to collect the card—but don’t promise a final payment link either.


11:41 AM






 is there a way you can answer this question without actually having me create a booking? 






11:42 AM






Worked for 5m 43s



Yes—and I completed the read-only audit.
Current conclusion:
Odysseus supports creating holds, taking payment later, extending payment, and sending booking emails.
Those are separate capabilities. Send Email does not prove Send Customer a Payment Link.
The tested MSC checkout reported hosted-payment mode disabled.
Therefore, we should currently assume a customer-operated final payment link is unavailable—not that it is impossible platform-wide.
We can settle it definitively without creating anything by:
Opening an existing unpaid booking with a balance due.
Inspecting its Make Payment and Send Email actions or email preview without sending.
Checking whether the preview contains a clean-browser customer payment URL.
If no suitable existing booking exists, ask Cruise Brothers support this exact question:
After placing an Odysseus cruise booking on hold without payment, can I send the customer a PCI-compliant payment URL that works in a clean browser without agent-session cookies? If so, where is it generated, and which cruise lines support it?
